This is NPR News Now. The latest headlines every hour.
Live from NPR News, I'm Charles Snyder. With less than two weeks to go until midterm
election day, President Trump was in North Carolina Tuesday night to support Republican
Michael Wadley, his hand-picked Senate candidate to replace outgoing Senator Tom Tillis.
Trump was in North Carolina for the second time in his many months urging North Carolina
Republicans to turn out on election day to keep Wadley's Democratic challenger,
former Governor Roy Cooper, from winning the seat. Polls show Cooper with the lead
in a Senate race that could help decide the balance of power in the chamber.
Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky says Ukraine is once again receiving early warnings
about Russian attacks. At a news conference in Oslo, Zelensky said the change happened after
Tuesday talks with his American counterparts, including a phone call with Secretary of State
Marco Rubio. Zelensky met with U.S. envoy Steve Whitcoff in Oslo. Whitcoff expected to meet with
Russian President Volodymyr Putin on Wednesday. Los Angeles County election officials say the
federal government's list of 20,000 likely non-citizens on California's voter rolls
appears to be unreliable. NPR's Jude Joffee Block reports on court filings by those county election
officials that some of the people on this appear to be born in the U.S. The Department of Justice
is demanding California take the unprecedented step of sequestering ballots associated with
20,000 people federal officials say are likely non-citizens. But the Los Angeles County
Registrar's Office analyzed a sample of 200 of the names on the list. They found records for some
people on the list indicated they were born in the U.S. and therefore may be American citizens.
70 percent of the sample had never voted before and 112 out of the 200 person sample were not
sent mailed ballots because their registrations were canceled or inactive. Jude Joffee Block, NPR News.
Streaming giant Netflix reporting slower quarterly revenue growth over the past three years and
PR's Mandalito Barco reports. Netflix co-CEO Greg Peters talked to investors after the third
quarter earnings report. Our engagement is solid but we know that we can do better. It's our goal
to go from very good to great. Peters said they had to make some tough financial decisions so last
week Netflix laid off a thousand workers, six percent of the company. After handing them their
pink slips the company's content chief was fired. Also ousted were the chairman of Netflix film and
six other top executives. The news comes at a turbulent time in Hollywood. Disney just had its
third wave of layoffs in six months and workers at the new Skydance company that merged Paramount
and Warner Brothers are bracing for massive layoffs too. Mandalito Barco, NPR News, Los Angeles.
This is NPR News. The man accused of ramming his car into Australian lawmaker Helen Haynes
was in court Wednesday. According to court filings, 43-year-old Brendan Nugent is charged with multiple
offenses including intentionally causing serious injury and causing harm to a public official.
Nugent did not apply for bail and is due to return to court in February. Haynes remains in
critical condition after doctors amputated one of her legs. China says it has sent forces to watch
a U.S. warship that inter-disputed waters around the Sabina Shoal in the South China Sea. The Shoal
is claimed by several countries and the surrounding waters have become a flashpoint for regional
tensions from Taipei, Jan Kamas and Brumby reports. The Chinese accused the USS Charleston of quote
"illegally entering the waters around Sabina Shoal". They accused the U.S. of infringing on Beijing's
sovereignty as well as undermining stability in the region. The Philippines meanwhile says the
U.S. ship did not enter Chinese territory adding that the vessel is traveling in international
waters. The United States has previously been known to carry out so-called freedom of navigation
operations in the region. Further north in the South China Sea, Taiwan reports a standoff with
a Chinese vessel around the Taiwan-controlled Pratas Island. For NVR News, I'm Jan Kamas and Brumby
in Taipei. China also criticizing a U.S. ban on the AI startup Deepsea. The Homeland Security
Department has ordered all federal civilian agencies to remove Deepsea products from their
systems over concerns about potential data access by Chinese authorities. China's commerce ministry
said Tuesday that "Beijing will take all necessary measures to safeguard its interests." This message
comes from Angie. Angie has been helping homeowners find skilled pros to get their home projects
done well for over 30 years. For everything from minor repairs to major remodels, find reviews,
pricing and booking at Angie.com or on the Angie app.
